# Pin how the progress, country-flag and GitHub-user grid columns map a record

## Welcome 👋

Some of Neo's grid columns render a small component in every cell: a progress bar, a country flag, a GitHub avatar. Each column has one method, `applyRecordConfigs(config, record)`, that turns a row's data into that component's configs. The mapping is tiny and untested. It is also exactly what you would change to build your own column.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Sources: `src/grid/column/Progress.mjs`, `CountryFlag.mjs`, `GitHubUser.mjs`
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/RecordConfigs.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/Component.spec.mjs` (creating a column with `Neo.create()` and giving it a `dataField`). A plain object works as the record for these methods.

## What to cover

| Column | `applyRecordConfigs(config, record)` returns |
|---|---|
| `Progress` | `{value: record[dataField]}` |
| `CountryFlag` | `{countryCode: record[dataField], location: record[contentField]}`, where `contentField` defaults to `'location'` |
| `GitHubUser` | `{avatarUrl: record.avatarUrl, username: record.login, fullName}`: `fullName` is `record.name`, or `''` when the name is missing or equals the login |
| all three | a key passed in `config` wins over the record-derived one (it is spread last) |

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/grid/column/RecordConfigs.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per column, plus the "`config` wins" row for each.
- [ ] Test-only: if a column disagrees with its row, say so on this issue before changing `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/column/RecordConfigs.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

Rendering inside a real grid, and the components themselves (`src/component/Progress.mjs` and friends).

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.
